title: Sep 22 Results + Sep 23 Preview: 60% Win Rate? We'll Take It (But We Want More)
summary: 9-6 on Sep 22 with some brutal misses. Tomorrow we ride with Detroit and Framber.

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest: 60% Is Good, But Those Misses Hurt

Look, I'm not going to sugarcoat this—9-6 is a winning day, and if you're complaining about a 60% hit rate, you don't understand sports betting. But let's talk about the *how* we got here, because some of these results were absolutely maddening.

We called 15 games yesterday and cashed on 9 of them. The wins? Clean. The losses? A few of them felt like the baseball gods were personally laughing at us. When you miss on a 61% Cubs pick at home, you start questioning everything. When the Rangers let us down at 50%? Well, that's just a coin flip that landed wrong.

But here's the thing—we're still profitable, we're still sharp, and tomorrow we've got a pick that I'm genuinely excited about.

## The Brutal Breakdown: What Went Right and Wrong

Here's where things get spicy. Our highest confidence picks went 1-2. That Cubs loss at 61%? Absolutely brutal. The Tigers miss at 62%? That one stings too. But the Pirates at 62%? Money in the bank.

The mid-range picks (50-54%) actually saved us, going 3-3. When you're betting close-to-even games, you expect variance. What you don't expect is your slam-dunk favorites to let you down.

The double-header Rays picks were perfect chaos—we went 1-1, which is basically the baseball gods telling us they have no idea what they're doing either.

## Tomorrow's Play: Detroit Tigers Are the Move

Let me be crystal clear about something—when Framber Valdez is on the mound, you pay attention. The Tigers are getting him at home against the Nationals, who are trotting out Richard Lovelady. No disrespect to Lovelady, but this is a mismatch.

Framber has been one of the most underrated arms in baseball, and the Tigers offense has shown they can do damage at home. Washington is playing out the string at this point in September. The model gives us 61% confidence, and honestly? I think that's conservative.

This is the kind of spot where you lean in, not pull back. Tomorrow's slate might have other games, but if you're looking for the sharpest play, it's Detroit. Period.

## The Bottom Line

We went 9-6 yesterday and made money. If you faded us, you left cash on the table. If you tailed every pick, you're up units. Tomorrow we're backing the Tigers with Framber on the bump, and I'm not losing sleep over it.

60% is good. Tomorrow we're chasing better.

*Let's ride.*
